record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: How can hydrodynamic behavior remain applicable in small and dilute collision systems, including proton-proton and proton-nucleus events, where the mean free path relative to system size and the number of collisions per particle appear to fall outside the usual hydrodynamic regime?

evidence.quote: Were it not for the difficulty to conceive of hydrodynamic behaviour not only in small and dense, but also in small and dilute systems, where hydro is thought to be well outside its range of applicability (mean free path/system size << 1 and #collisions/particle << 1, see however [40]), the well-motivated but increasingly Ptolemaic CGC explanation would have had to concede defeat a while ago, given the clear preponderance of evidence.

While hydrodynamic codes can and are being used in ever smaller systems, down to pp at LHC, and actually give very consistent and coherent results well in line with the data, the debate does (and should) continue until we do understand the causes and the actual dynamics behind what is yet another case for an unreasonably successful model (hydro in small dilute systems).
What is the underlying dynamics, which makes thermalisation (if really achieved?) seemingly so fast, including in small and possibly even in dilute systems?

artifact.category_tag: Relativistic hydrodynamics in small collision systems
artifact.status_search_result: The applicability and microscopic justification of hydrodynamics in small, dilute pp and pA systems remains an active and unresolved research topic. Recent works (e.g., 2024–2025 studies on partonic collectivity at the LHC, light-ion collision programs, hydrodynamic attractor analyses, and characterizations of the initial state for hydrodynamics in pp/pA) continue to debate the mechanism, with no consensus explanation. The question is therefore considered open.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing the initial state of hydrodynamics in pp and pA collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Hydrodynamic-like behavior in pp and pA collisions presents a conceptual problem of how the initial state of such a hydrodynamic evolution should be characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Active debate in 2025 over how to justify and initialize hydrodynamics in small systems.

status_evidence.title: Exploring the partonic collectivity in small systems at the LHC
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of elliptic flow in high-multiplicity pp and p-Pb collisions continue, with model-dependent conclusions about the onset of collectivity.
status_evidence.claim: Mechanism behind collectivity in small systems is still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: High Multiplicity pp and pA Collisions: Hydrodynamics at its Edge
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses why hydrodynamics appears to apply at the edge of its expected validity in small systems.
status_evidence.claim: Long-standing open question regarding hydrodynamic applicability in small dilute systems.
